title: Calibrating Humanity's Last Exam as a Safety Capability Proxy

original_idea.title: Calibrating Humanity's Last Exam as a Safety Capability Proxy
original_idea.problem: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) is designed to measure extreme expert-level knowledge, but its relationship to safety-relevant capabilities (e.g., synthesizing dangerous knowledge) has not been examined.
original_idea.direction: Identify the subset of HLE questions that touch on safety-sensitive domains (chemistry, biology, nuclear physics, cybersecurity). Evaluate 2–3 open-source models on these subsets. Compare performance on safety-sensitive HLE items to refusal rates on matched harmful prompts from AILuminate or ForesightSafety Bench. Test whether high performance on safety-sensitive knowledge correlates with higher harm rates.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Capability benchmarks and safety benchmarks are usually run separately. If high capability in dangerous knowledge domains correlates with higher harm rates, then capability benchmarks have direct safety implications.
original_idea.relevant_context: Humanity's Last Exam is a key dataset in the subfield context. The capability-safety relationship is a core concern in AI safety evaluation design and has been addressed in WMDP but not in HLE.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: connecting capability benchmarks to safety outcomes would bridge two separate evaluation paradigms. If correlation exists, it changes how capability benchmarks are interpreted.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires accessing HLE dataset, identifying safety-sensitive subsets, and running correlation analysis across two different benchmarks. Moderate complexity requiring some statistical knowledge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Running two different benchmarks and correlating results adds scope. Identifying the safety-sensitive HLE subset is a sub-task itself. Could be narrowed to one domain (e.g., chemistry only).

novelty.reasoning: Humanity's Last Exam is widely used as a capability benchmark but no existing work examines its relationship to safety-relevant capabilities. WMDP addresses capability-safety relationships for dangerous knowledge domains but not via HLE. The specific idea of identifying safety-sensitive HLE subsets and correlating performance with harm rates on safety benchmarks is novel.
